name: AI Deep Dive — SKHY — 2026-07-13
rationale: SK Hynix (SKHY) completed its Nasdaq listing in July 2026, raising $26.5B and establishing a direct trading vehicle for U.S. retail and institutional investors. As the clear pioneer and current market leader in High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM3/HBM3e) supply for Nvidia's AI compute platforms, the company enjoys superior yield rates and margin profiles compared to peers. This projection models a base case CAGR of 45% over 5 years, transitioning HBM leadership into sustained long-term earnings power, while the bear case models a standard cyclical consolidation starting in FY2028.

bear.rationale: Bear case assumes standard memory cycle down-turn. HBM capacity expansion from Samsung and Micron creates supply parity by FY2028, compressing ASPs from premium levels. 15% CAGR yields Year 5 revenue of $144.8B, with net margins mean-reverting to 8% and exit P/E at 12x.
risks: Samsung succeeds in qualifying HBM3e for Nvidia, eroding SK Hynix's dominant supplier status
Hyperscaler capex consolidation reduces HBM pricing power

base.rationale: Base case assumes SK Hynix maintains its lead in HBM3e/HBM4 yield rates, securing ~50% of global HBM market share. 45% CAGR yields Year 5 revenue of $461.5B, with net margin averaging 22% and exit P/E at 22x, reflecting premium status as the top Nvidia memory partner.
risks: Semi cycle downturn in late 2028 slows capex growth

bull.rationale: Bull case assumes HBM shortages persist through 2031, sustaining high-margin premium pricing. SK Hynix remains Nvidia's primary partner for next-generation platforms, yielding 55% CAGR, 30% net margin, and 28x exit P/E.
risks: Extreme macro shock to global supply chain in APAC region

aiThesis.rationale: SK Hynix is the clear market leader in HBM, holding a dominant position in the Nvidia supply chain. The Nasdaq listing establishes a direct vehicle for US investors. Fair value is highly dependent on HBM shortage duration.
